item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: EPH Invest set a 1-for-20 share consolidation scenario alongside a planned capital increase, pending an extraordinary shareholder vote. Share count would fall to 5,618,405 from 112,368,105, with share capital unchanged at EUR 2.7 million. The planned in-kind capital increase would issue up to 679,469 new shares post-consolidation, or 13,589,431 pre-consolidation. Issue price set at EUR 1.45 per new share post-consolidation, or EUR 0.07 pre-consolidation, implying up to about 10.79% dilution. Capital increase sized at up to EUR 985,228.60 post-consolidation, or EUR 985,233.75 pre-consolidation, mainly for creditor conversion and SPV stakes. item.title: Episurf accelerates shift to pure-play property company, winds down medtech operations
item.description: Episurf Medical will accelerate its shift into a pure-play Nordic property company, reallocating capital and resources to its real estate platform. The boar
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Episurf Medical will accelerate its shift into a pure-play Nordic property company, reallocating capital and resources to its real estate platform. The board launched an orderly wind-down of the operating medtech business, citing weak feasibility and high time and capital demands for a sale or spin-off. Focus will shift to monetizing the patent portfolio and other intangible assets, rather than continuing in-house production and operations. FDA feedback in the Episealer MTP 510(k) process called for additional validation data, increasing required investment and timelines for US clearance. The medtech wind-down is expected to lower the cost base, supporting earnings from Q2 2027. item.title: Metal Energy says charter aircraft makes emergency landing near Prince George; vehicle occupant killed
item.description: Metal Energy confirmed two exploration employees were on a charter aircraft that made an emergency landing near Prince George, B.C., on Aug. 20, 2026. The a
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Metal Energy confirmed two exploration employees were on a charter aircraft that made an emergency landing near Prince George, B.C., on Aug. 20, 2026. The aircraft struck several vehicles during the landing; an occupant of one vehicle died. The company’s employees were uninjured; the pilot and other passengers were also unharmed. The flight was rotating crews from the NIV copper-gold-molybdenum project in British Columbia’s Toodoggone District. Transportation Safety Board of Canada investigation is ongoing; Metal Energy is supporting staff, cooperating with authorities, limiting further comment.
